title: Lawyers push for Momay's recognition as 58th Maguindanao Massacre victim
summary: Lawyers representing families of the victims of the 2009 Maguindanao massacre on Monday urged the Court of Appeals (CA) to recognize photojournalist Reynaldo “Bebot” Momay as the 58th victim of the…

blocks.text: Lawyers representing families of the victims of the 2009 Maguindanao massacre on Monday urged the Court of Appeals (CA) to recognize photojournalist Reynaldo “Bebot” Momay as the 58th victim of the killings, 17 years after the gruesome incident.

Center for International Law (CenterLaw) Philippines executive director Gilbert Andres filed a second motion for resolution before the appellate court on behalf of 19 families, seeking action on pending appeals involving the massacre, including the legal recognition of Momay and the release of civil damages.

Momay, a photojournalist for the Tacurong-based Midland Review, was among those who joined the convoy of journalists and supporters of then gubernatorial candidate Esmael Mangudadatu on Nov. 23, 2009. His remains, however, were never recovered.
"Ang aming hinhiling na talagang i-recognize na kasama si Momay sa mga pinaslang sa Sitio Masalay, Ampatuan, Maguindanao. Ang mga biktima ay may right to truth and right to justice," Andres said.

"Sa totoo lang, noong panahon na yun, my youngest son is only nine. Ngayon, may apo na ako sa kanya. Pero hanggang ngayon, nag-aantay pa rin kami ng hustisya; kahit man lang ina-acknowledge ang tatay ko, di pa magawa," said Reynafe, Momay's daughter.
Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda also urged the CA to resolve the pending appeals with dispatch, stressing that the victims' families have waited long enough for justice.
Andres welcomed the chief justice's call, saying it reinforced the families' appeal for the court to act on the long-pending cases.

Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda on Monday urged the Court of Appeals (CA) to promptly resolve the pending appeals in the Maguindanao massacre case, as the country marked the 17th anniversary of the tragedy.

Speaking at his first flag-raising ceremony as Chief Justice, Zalameda said the victims and their families had waited long enough for justice, stressing that the proceedings should no longer be delayed.

“As we speak of protecting those who stand for justice, we must also remember the victims of the Ampatuan Massacre, whose 17th anniversary we commemorate today. The victims and their families have waited long enough,” Zalameda said.

“I therefore urge the Court of Appeals to resolve the pending appeals with dispatch, consistent with due process and rights of all parties. Let us ensure that justice is not delayed any further,” he added.

The Maguindanao massacre, also known as the Ampatuan massacre, took place on Nov. 23, 2009, when a convoy carrying relatives and supporters of then Buluan Vice Mayor Esmael Mangudadatu, along with journalists and other civilians, was ambushed in Ampatuan town, Maguindanao.

The victims were accompanying Mangudadatu’s wife, Genalyn, and other family members as they were on their way to file his certificate of candidacy for the 2010 gubernatorial elections. Fifty-seven people were killed in the attack, including 32 journalists and media workers, making it the deadliest single attack on journalists in history. —LDF, GMA News
